chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Husayn al-Sayqal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

'God does not accept a deed except with understanding, and there is no understanding except with a deed. So whoever has understanding, the understanding guides him toward the deed; and whoever does not act, has no understanding. Indeed! Faith — part of it is from another part.'

key_terms.الإيمان: Iman — faith as a lived, integrated reality encompassing belief, knowledge, and action
key_terms.عمل: 'Amal — righteous deed, religious practice, action in accordance with divine command
key_terms.معرفة: Ma'rifa — deep religious knowledge and recognition of God, the Imam, and obligations; more than surface information

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between knowledge and deeds in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the inseparable unity between religious knowledge (ma'rifa) and righteous action ('amal). This teaching was addressed to early Shia students who needed to understand that theoretical knowledge alone is insufficient — true gnosis necessarily manifests in conduct. The closing statement that 'faith is interconnected within itself' echoes a key Shia theological position that iman is a unified, organically integrated reality rather than a mere verbal declaration.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, fromHusayn Al Sayqal who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘Allahazwj does not Accept a deed except with the understanding, nor the understanding except with the deed. So the one who understands that, the understanding would indicate him upon the (performance of the) deed, and the one who does not act, so there is no understanding for him. Indeed! The Eman, part of it is from the other part’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Hassan al-Sayqal who has said the following. “(Imam) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.)

who has said, “Allah does not accept a deed without good understanding and proper understanding does not come into being without work. One who achieves proper understanding it will guide him to good deeds and one who does not work will not have any understanding. Is it not a fact that parts of faith comes from other parts?”
